headline: Florida International University in Miami will install a 256-qubit IonQ quantum computer on its campus, the first of its kind in Florida.
score_reason: Contract signed 23 Sep and announced 24 Sep 2026, before the window; machine not due until end of 2027.
importance_line: Students, researchers and local industry gain access to quantum hardware, but not for more than a year and terms are undisclosed.
summary: CiberCuba reports that Florida International University has signed a deal with IonQ, a US quantum computing company, to install a 256-qubit trapped-ion system called Superion 256, expected by the end of 2027. The contract was signed on 23 Sep 2026 and its financial terms were not disclosed, and the university must first finish a secure data centre to house it.
notes: Original (The Business Journals) blocked; read CiberCuba's report of the same announcement; url is CiberCuba page.
